mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over a 3-month window signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or if the mechanism fails during a recession (UNRATE < 2%) despite the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or if the mechanism fails during periods of simultaneous strong GDP growth (GDPC1 q/q > 3%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS shows two consecutive monthly declines
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or if GDP growth (GDPC1 q/q) is simultaneously positive and above 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between rising FEDFUNDS and falling CPIAUCSL (inflation) over a 3-month window signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising AND CPIAUCSL falling over 3 months
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or if the mechanism fails when unemployment is rising (UNRATE monthly change < -0.2%).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their respective 12-month averages signals a broad-based labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-mo avg AND UNRATE > 12-mo avg for 1 month
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or if GDP growth (GDPC1 q/q) is negative at the time of trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or if mortgage rates (not available but implied via FEDFUNDS) are rising sharply at the same time.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) of more than 1% signals a macroeconomic downturn, which reduces corporate earnings and cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or if the decline is not accompanied by rising unemployment (UNRATE monthly change > -0.1%).
